title: Follow a GPU request from admission to a healthy device
description: Select a scheduling or runtime condition to see which control-plane and node components participate, where the request stops, and what the workload observes.

nodes.label: GPU Pod
nodes.detail: Declares an integer accelerator limit, host CPU and memory, eligible hardware labels, tolerations, topology constraints, priority, and a restart policy.

nodes.label: Scheduler
nodes.detail: Filters nodes by allocatable resources and placement policy, scores the remaining nodes, and records one Pod-to-node binding. It does not initialize the GPU.

nodes.label: Kubelet
nodes.detail: Watches the binding, asks the registered device plugin to allocate healthy device IDs, and prepares the Pod through the container runtime.

nodes.label: Device plugin
nodes.detail: Registers a vendor resource with the kubelet, reports healthy devices, and returns device allocation instructions for an admitted container.

nodes.label: Container runtime
nodes.detail: Creates the container with the allocated device nodes, libraries, mounts, and environment supplied by the plugin and vendor runtime integration.

nodes.label: GPU or partition
nodes.detail: Executes the workload under whole-device, MIG-profile, or time-sliced semantics. Device memory, fault isolation, and performance guarantees depend on that mode.

scenarios.label: Whole-GPU success
scenarios.summary: The Pod requests one vendor GPU, matches a labeled and tolerated node, and receives one healthy exclusive device.
scenarios.result: The container starts with the assigned device. Scheduling success proves resource allocation, so readiness must still check that the model, driver, runtime, and application initialized correctly.

scenarios.label: No eligible profile
scenarios.summary: Free accelerator capacity exists, but no node has the model, MIG profile, zone, and tolerations required by the Pod.
scenarios.result: The Pod remains Pending. Inspect scheduler events and the complete eligibility intersection; adding an incompatible GPU node does not resolve the constraint.

scenarios.label: Device becomes unhealthy
scenarios.summary: The vendor plugin stops reporting one device as healthy after an error, reducing allocatable capacity on the node.
scenarios.result: New Pods must not receive that device. Existing workload recovery depends on the application, controller, checkpoint, node remediation, and vendor behavior; Kubernetes does not migrate GPU process memory.

scenarios.label: Time-slice contention
scenarios.summary: Several Pods receive shared resource tokens for one physical GPU and then compete for compute and device memory.
scenarios.result: All Pods can be Running while latency and memory pressure degrade. Time slicing shares access; it does not provide MIG-style memory or fault isolation or a proportional compute entitlement.
